content: 1. Brekke KR, Holmas TH, and Straume OR conducted a study on reference pricing, competition, and pharmaceutical expenditures, providing both theoretical insights and evidence from a natural experiment. This was published in the Journal of Public Economics in 2011, volume 95, issues 7-8, pages 624-638. 2. Do Amaral SMS and Blatt CR examined the impact of municipal consortia for medicine procurement on stockouts and budgets. Their findings were published in Revista de Saúde Pública in 2011, volume 45, issue 4, pages 799-801. 3. Kohler JC, Mitsakakis N, Saadat F, Byng D, and Martinez MG explored whether pharmaceutical pricing transparency matters by analyzing Brazil’s public procurement system. Their work appeared in Global Health in 2015, volume 11, article 34. 4. Grootendorst PV, Marshall JK, Holbrook AM, Dolovich LR, O'Brien BJ, and Levy AR investigated the effects of differential cost-sharing of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs on the use and costs of analgesic medications. This research was part of the Social and Economic Dimensions of an Aging Population Research Paper series in 2004, paper 115, pages 1-38. 5. Kaiser U, Mendez SJ, and Ronde T studied the regulation of pharmaceutical prices, presenting evidence from a reference price reform in Denmark. Their findings were published as part of the CIE Discussion Papers at the University of Copenhagen in 2010, spanning 31 pages. 6. Kalo Z, Muszbek N, Bodrogi J, and Bidlo J analyzed whether therapeutic reference pricing consistently leads to cost containment, using evidence from Hungary. Their study was published in Health Policy in 2007, volume 80, issue 3, pages 402-412. 7. Toulemon L investigated the effects of regional purchasing groups on hospital medicine prices, using evidence from group formations. This study was published in HAL in 2017, covering pages 1-34. 8. Habl C, Leopold C, Schmickl B, and Fröschl B provided an executive summary on reference price systems in Europe. This report was published in Vienna in 2008 as a PDF document. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) examined the impact of tax exemption measures on the prices of oncology medications in 2010, though no statistical analysis was included. 10. Puig-Junoy J reviewed the financing and price regulation of drugs within the Spanish National Health System, highlighting changes and continuity. This study was published in Gaceta Sanitaria in 2007, volume 21, issue 1, pages 1-4. 11. Festic M analyzed cost containment strategies for public pharmaceutical expenditures in the European Union, with an English summary included. This was published in Nase Gospodarstvo/Our Economy in 2004, volume 50, issues 1-2, pages 84-92. 12. Lannuzel X discussed the fixed responsibility tariff or reference price system as a measure for controlling healthcare expenditures in Europe and France. This publication from 2008 is unavailable. 13. Lichert F studied the effects of price-cap regulations on price development. This research was published in Gesundheitswesen in 2015, volume 20, issue 6, pages 250-251, but the publication is unavailable. 14. Bigdeli M and Annear PL identified barriers to access and the role of health equity funds in Cambodia, focusing on lessons learned. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2009, volume 87, issue 7, pages 560-564. 15. Tu HT and Lauer JR examined the impact of healthcare price transparency on price variation, using the New Hampshire experience as a case study. This was published as an issue brief in 2009, issue 128, pages 1-4. 16. Yoshida K and Kawahara K conducted a comparative study on the impact of a fixed price system on the supply of institutional long-term care in Japanese and German metropolitan areas. Their findings were published in BMC Health Services Research in 2014, volume 14, article 48. 17. Modoux F reported on drug pricing trends, noting a reduction of 4-5%. This was published in Revue Médicale Suisse in 2015, volume 11, issue 473, page 1046. 18. Silversides A discussed monitoring the prices of new drugs in a news report published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal in 2006, volume 174, issue 11, pages 1548-1549. 19. Wang L, Yu JJ, Zhou BM, Li YP, Cheng L, Yuan Q, et al. conducted a systematic review of national drug policies in seventeen countries. Their findings were published in the Chinese Journal of Evidence-Based Medicine in 2009, volume 9, issue 7, pages 715-729.
